subsidyProgram.name: National Fertilizer Subsidy Programme
howToRegister: Visit your nearest chief's office or agricultural extension officer
Register as a farmer on the eCitizen platform (ecitizen.go.ke)
Provide national ID, KRA PIN, and land ownership/lease documents
Specify the acreage under cultivation and crops grown
Once approved, you receive SMS notifications when fertilizer is available
Collect from designated NCPB depots with your national ID
eligibility: Must be a Kenyan citizen with valid national ID
Must be a registered farmer (subsistence or commercial)
Land size verification required (maximum allocation depends on acreage)
Maximum allocation: 100 bags per farmer per season (subject to availability)

fertilizers.name: DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate)
fertilizers.use: Basal/planting fertilizer. High phosphorus for root development.
fertilizers.application: Apply at planting — 1 bag per acre for maize. Place 5cm below and beside the seed.

fertilizers.name: CAN (Calcium Ammonium Nitrate)
fertilizers.use: Top-dressing fertilizer. Provides nitrogen for vegetative growth.
fertilizers.application: Apply as top-dress when maize is knee-height (4–6 weeks after planting). Side-dress 5cm from plant stem.

fertilizers.name: NPK (23-23-0)
fertilizers.use: Balanced planting fertilizer with both nitrogen and phosphorus.
fertilizers.application: Apply at planting. Good alternative to DAP where nitrogen is also needed at planting.

fertilizers.name: Urea
fertilizers.use: High-nitrogen top-dressing fertilizer. Most concentrated nitrogen source.
fertilizers.application: Top-dress only — never apply at planting (burns seeds). Apply when soil is moist. Loses nitrogen if left on surface — incorporate immediately.

fertilizers.name: TSP (Triple Super Phosphate)
fertilizers.use: Pure phosphorus fertilizer for phosphorus-deficient soils.
fertilizers.application: Apply at planting. Best for acidic soils that fix phosphorus from DAP.

fertilizers.name: MOP (Muriate of Potash)
fertilizers.use: Potassium fertilizer for fruit development, disease resistance, and water regulation.
fertilizers.application: Apply at planting or as a split application. Important for fruiting crops and potatoes.

notes: Subsidized prices are set by the government and may change each planting season. Confirm current prices at your nearest NCPB depot.
Market prices are approximate — they fluctuate based on global fertilizer commodity markets and exchange rates.
The subsidy programme may have stock limitations. Register early (2–3 months before planting season) to secure allocation.
Always buy from licensed agrovets or NCPB depots. Counterfeit fertilizer is a serious problem — check packaging seals and KEBS certification.
Soil testing is recommended before applying fertilizer. Contact KALRO for soil testing services (KES 500–1,500 per sample).
